item.text: {"question_id":"7B.5","answer":"For 2023, Tshisekedi’s appointments and removals show a formally lawful but materially opaque and contested record. He directly reshuffled the cabinet, appointed nine Gécamines board and management members, and issued extensive judicial orders promoting, appointing, dismissing, compulsorily retiring, and reassigning magistrates (BATCH-0009-E003; BATCH-0018-E004; BATCH-0015-E006; BATCH-0019-E005; BATCH-0019-E006). Official accounts present these actions as judicial reform and national-resource management, but provide no individual qualifications, selection criteria, reasons for removals, performance evidence, or independent assessment of judicial independence. Adverse reporting states that Tshisekedi moved to place sympathetic judges in key institutions, including appointing a Kasaïan head of the Constitutional Court, and reports allegations of ethnic stacking; ACLED separately records widespread concerns that the CENI was politically close to the government and that Denis Kadima was viewed by critics as close to Tshisekedi. These sources establish presidential attribution and a credible patronage or loyalty concern, but several claims remain allegations or reported perceptions rather than adjudicated findings, and they do not prove appointments were made to protect personal self-dealing. The 2024 analysis of UDPS loyalists and technocrats is excluded from material characterization of the 2023 period because of its later period
